lead: Kansas plumbing deals with hard water, clay soils, storms and cold winters. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers from Wichita to Overland Park.
risk: hard water scale, frozen pipes and sewer lines cracked by shifting soil
risk_short: hard water, frozen pipes and sewer lines
why: Kansas water is often hard, scaling up water heaters and fixtures. Clay soils swell and shrink with rain and drought, which stresses sewer lines and foundations.
Winter cold snaps freeze pipes, and spring storms bring flooding. Kansas has no statewide plumber license; cities and counties such as Wichita and Sedgwick County license plumbers.
tips: Test your sump pump before spring.
areas: Calls come from Wichita, Overland Park, Kansas City, Olathe, Topeka, Lawrence, Manhattan and rural Kansas.

faq.q: Do plumbers need a license in Kansas?
faq.a: There is no statewide plumber license. Cities and counties license plumbers and issue permits, so check with your local building department.
